'''Franz Joachim Wegner''' (born 15 June 1940) is emeritus professor for [[theoretical physics]] at the [[University of Heidelberg]].

==Education==
Franz Wegner attained a doctorate in 1968 with thesis advisor Wilhelm Brenig at the [[Technical University of Munich]] with the thesis, "Zum Heisenberg-Modell im paramagnetischen Bereich und am kritischen Punkt" ("On the [[Heisenberg model (quantum)|Heisenberg model]] within the paramagnetic range and at the critical point").

Subsequently, he did research with a post-doctoral position at [[Forschungszentrum Jülich]], in the group of [[Herbert Wagner (physicist)|Herbert Wagner]] and at [[Brown University]] with [[Leo Kadanoff]].<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Kadanoff, L. P.|author2=Wegner, F. J.|title=Some Critical Properties of the Eight-Vertex Model|journal=Phys. Rev. B|year=1971|volume=4|issue=11|pages=3989–93|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.4.3989|bibcode = 1971PhRvB...4.3989K }}</ref> Since 1974 he is a professor at Heidelberg University.<ref name="pt76">{{citation|title=German Physical Society gives theoretical-physics awards|journal=[[Physics Today]]|volume=29|issue=9|year=1976|doi=10.1063/1.3023914|page=69|bibcode = 1976PhT....29i..69. }}.</ref>

==Research==
The emphasis of Wegner's scientific work is [[statistical physics]], in particular the theory of [[phase transition]]s and the [[renormalization group]].<ref>{{citation|title=From order to chaos II: essays, critical, chaotic, and otherwise|volume=32|series=Series on Nonlinear Science|first=Leo P.|last=Kadanoff|publisher=World Scientific|year=1999|isbn=978-981-02-3434-8|page=161|bibcode=1999fotc.book.....K |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uFsnv27G5M8C&pg=PA161}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Conceptual Foundations of Quantum Field Theory|first=Tian Yu|last=Cao|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=2004|isbn=978-0-521-60272-3|page=93|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=d0wS0EJHZ3MC&pg=PA93}}.</ref> The eponymous "Wegner exponent" is of fundamental importance for the purpose of describing corrections to asymptotic scale invariance in close proximity to phase transitions. Wegner also "invented"  the foundational [[Lattice gauge theory|lattice gauge theoretical]] models. The method developed from Wegner's foundational work is nowadays intensively used in simulations of [[quantum chromodynamics]].

==Accolades==
Wegner won the [[Walter Schottky Prize|Walter Schottky prize]] in 1976 for his work on phase transitions and elementary particles.<ref name="pt76"/> He has also been elected to the Heidelberger Academy of Sciences and won the [[Max Planck medal]] among other awards and recognitions. He won the [[Lars Onsager Prize|Lars Onsager prize]] from [[American Physical Society]] in 2015 for his contributions to Statistical mechanics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Wegner&first_nm=Franz&year=2015|title=Prize Recipient|website=aps.org|language=en|access-date=2018-01-30}}</ref>
